newsitem.title: USA: Lilly's Humatrope recommended for approval.
newsitem.headline: Lilly's Humatrope recommended for approval.

text.p: Eli Lilly and Co said Wednesday that its Humatrope for injection was recommended by a U.S. Food and Drug Administration panel for marketing clearance for short stature associated with Turner Syndrome.
The recommended was made by a six-to-one vote by the FDA's Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee.
The committee's recommendation, while not binding, will be considered by the FDA in its final review of the supplemental new drug application submitted by Lilly in July 1996.
Lilly said it and Genentech Inc jointly presented medical data on their respective human growth hormone products for short stature associated with Turner Syndrome before the FDA advisory committee,
Lilly said Genentech's human growth hormone, Nutropin, also received a positive recommendation by the FDA advisory committee.

Lilly and Genentech each filed drug applications independently with the FDA for human growth hormone for short stature associated with Turner Syndrome. The two companies have agreed to share orphan drug exclusivity for human growth hormone for the Turner Syndrome indication only.

Humatrope is a synthetic human growth hormone that has been used since 1987 as a replacement therapy for children who do not produce enough or any of their own hormone. In August 1996, the FDA cleared Humatrope for marketing to treat Somatropin Deficiency Syndrome in adults.
Humatrope already has been cleared for marketing in more than 30 countries for short stature associated with Turner Syndrome.
